title: How to write instructions for an AI agent | 50agents
description: Write AI agent instructions like a job description: the job, the cases, the steps, the output, the reason behind each rule, and what to do when unsure.
h1: How to write instructions for an AI agent
answer: Write them like a job description for a careful new hire: the job, its cases, the steps, the output, and what to do when unsure.
Give the reason behind each rule, and retest on real cases after every change.

body.p: Seven short parts, in this order. Most AI agents need 100 to 250 words; if yours runs past a page, it is probably two jobs.

head: Part
What to write
Example (support replies)
rows: Reply to questions sent to support@
What it handles, what it leaves
Orders and returns; leave complaints to me
Read, look up the order, draft
Returns policy and delivery times in memory
Don't draft; say what is missing
A wrong promise costs more than delay

ul: **Before:** "Be helpful and answer customer emails." **After:** "Reply to order, delivery and returns questions sent to support@. Leave complaints and refunds for me."
**Before:** "NEVER make anything up." **After:** "Answer only from the returns policy in memory. If the answer is not there, tell me what is missing."
**Before:** "Keep it short." **After:** "Under 120 words. First name in the greeting. No bullet points."
**Before:** "Handle edge cases." **After:** "If there is no order number, ask for it in one line."

method.h2: How to write instructions for an AI agent

steps.title: Start from what you already tell people
steps.body: Your returns policy, the email you send new staff, your canned replies. Paste them in as facts; do not rewrite them from memory.

steps.title: Write the job and the cases first
steps.body: One sentence for the job, then what it handles and what it leaves. Most bad AI agents fail here, not in the details.

steps.title: Number the steps
steps.body: One action per step, each tied to a clear output. If a step says "and", it is probably two.

note.text: Models take requests literally. "Suggest changes" may get you suggestions and no changes. Say whether it should act or only propose.

steps.title: Describe the output exactly
steps.body: Length, tone, greeting, sign-off, format. Paste one good example if you have it.

steps.title: Give the reason, drop the capitals
steps.body: "A voice engine cannot read ellipses" works better than "never use ellipses". Newer models follow closely, so "CRITICAL: you MUST" makes them overdo it.

note.text: A bare rule with no reason gets applied too literally, in cases where it was never meant to apply.

steps.title: Write the unsure line
steps.body: What it does when facts are missing, the case is unclear, or a search finds nothing. "Skip it and tell me why" is a good default.

steps.title: Test on 10 real cases
steps.body: Include the awkward ones. Change one thing at a time and rerun the same cases, so you know which change helped.

captain.line: Captain writes the first version of the instructions from your sentence and shows them on the plan. Later you change them by telling the AI agent in its chat.

wrong.title: It does more than you meant
wrong.body: The instructions said what to do but not what to leave. Add the cases it should not touch.

wrong.title: The important rule gets lost
wrong.body: The instructions grew to two pages. Cut what the AI agent never uses, and move reference facts into memory.

wrong.title: "Nothing found" when there was something
wrong.body: It searched the wrong way, such as for the word "unread" instead of the unread label. Tell it what to search, and to say what it searched when it finds nothing.

wrong.title: Changes break what worked
wrong.body: You fixed one case and broke another. Keep your 10 test cases and run all of them after each change.

faqs.q: How long should AI agent instructions be?
faqs.a: As short as covers the job, the cases, the steps, the output and the unsure case. For most small-business AI agents that is 100 to 250 words, plus reference facts kept separately.
One good example of the output helps a lot, especially for tone. Examples of inputs belong in your test set, not in the instructions.

faqs.q: What goes in instructions and what goes in memory?
faqs.a: Instructions say how to do the job. Memory holds facts that change: prices, policies, opening hours. Keeping them apart means you update a price without touching the job.
